panels.visual: Plato teaching students in a shady olive grove with a sacred shrine, scrolls and a drawing in the dust
panels.caption: Around 387 BC Plato started a school in a grove sacred to the hero Akademos. So it was called the Academy.

panels.visual: A modern city park with ruins and a tall apartment building behind, Glauka perched on a broken column
panels.caption: Every academy in the world since then is named after that grove.

panels.visual: Plato's bare shoulders in a wrestling match in a gym, sand, a crowd, comic scene with 'Platon' meaning broad
panels.caption: Platon means broad. Some say it came from his shoulders.

panels.visual: A sign above a school door reading LET NO ONE IGNORANT OF GEOMETRY ENTER, a student reading it, a question mark and a clock showing centuries
panels.caption: Nobody mentioned that sign until centuries later.
